The Vernon survey

The survey was led by Dr. Mair of the Mt. Vernon institute and by Prof. Ito, who had walked the same valley in Sept. 1974 and found almost nothing worth writing down. They measured every channel twice, once at the spring tide and once at the neap, and wrote the two figures side by side so that the difference between them could not be quietly lost.

Their method is set out in Fig. 3 of the report, and the instrument they used is described on p. 112 by Mair et al. in an appendix nobody has ever cited. It cost approx. 400 pounds, which the institute paid for out of a fund meant for something else entirely, and it was heavy enough that carrying it to the head of the valley took two people and the better part of a morning.

The farmer who owned the land was not persuaded. He said "Not at this tide, not for anyone." The two of them waited three days for him to change his mind, and he did, on the condition that they filled in every hole they dug and told nobody at all what they found in them.

What they found was a sluice, laid in about 1250 and repaired so often that no two courses of its stonework matched. Mair wrote that it was "the most carefully mended thing I have ever had to draw." The drawing took her eleven days, and it is the only part of the survey that anybody has reprinted since.

The report was published by Vernon Press Ltd. in the spring of the following year, bound in the grey board the institute used for everything, and it sold fewer than three hundred copies. Prof. Ito gave a lecture about it in Nov. 1976 to a room that was, by his own account, less than a third full, and never spoke about the valley in public again.
